text:
E. Werner Reschke criticizes Oregon’s Medicaid expansion and calls for new leadership
J. K. Goff
E. Werner Reschke, an Oregon state legislator, used his social media account to criticize the state's healthcare policies and leadership in a series of posts on August 10 and 11, 2026.
On August 10, Reschke posted: "We just continue to be the best at the worst. Oregon is Broken New Leadership Required Fix in November https://t.co/KxU9BHWJi8". This statement was made amid ongoing debates about the effectiveness of Oregon's political leadership and governance.
Later that day, he commented on Medicaid policy with another post: "When your state EXPANDS eligibility & coverage for Medicaid (Oregon Health Plan), but only pays out 50-65% of the cost of healthcare services, you might run into a problem like this: https://t.co/dHHCLy9gBz". In this message, Reschke highlighted concerns about the financial sustainability of expanding Medicaid coverage without fully funding service costs.
On August 11, Reschke shared another brief message referencing advice he endorsed: "Great advice https://t.co/DOpulmKU0F".
Oregon has expanded its Medicaid program under federal guidelines in recent years, increasing access to health insurance for low-income residents. However, some critics argue that reimbursement rates for providers remain lower than actual costs incurred by hospitals and clinics. This gap can create financial strain on healthcare providers across the state.
The timing of Reschke's remarks coincides with broader discussions among policymakers and voters ahead of upcoming elections in November 2026.
